name: Aceclofenac + Paracetamol
meta: Aceclofenac: Non-selective NSAID (phenylacetic acid derivative); Paracetamol (Acetaminophen): Non-opioid analgesic and antipyretic
Prescription-only fixed-dose combination. Components – Aceclofenac: Schedule H –
prescription only; Paracetamol (Acetaminophen): Non-prescription for plain low-strength oral forms; Schedule H in combinations
sections: Phenylacetic acid derivative (glycolic ester of diclofenac)
White crystalline powder, practically insoluble in water (BCS Class II).
White crystalline powder, odourless with bitter taste; melting point 169 °C; sparingly soluble in water.

Aceclofenac: A glycolic acid ester of diclofenac developed in Spain; widely used in Europe and India for osteoarthritis, RA and ankylosing spondylitis. First approval/introduction: Patented 1983; approved 1992 (Prodesfarma / Almirall, Spain). Paracetamol (Acetaminophen): On the WHO List of Essential Medicines and the most widely used analgesic–antipyretic worldwide; onset ~37 minutes after an oral dose. First approval/introduction: Synthesised 1877 (Harmon Northrop Morse); clinical use from 1887; widely marketed from 1950s.
Aceclofenac provides peripheral anti-inflammatory action; paracetamol adds central analgesia and antipyresis, giving faster and more complete pain relief.

Aceclofenac Inhibits cyclo-oxygenase (preferential COX-2) reducing prostaglandin synthesis; also inhibits IL-1 and TNF and stimulates cartilage matrix synthesis. Analgesic, anti-inflammatory and antipyretic. Receptor / target profile: Inhibits COX (preferential COX-2) and suppresses IL-1beta and TNF; stimulates glycosaminoglycan synthesis in cartilage.

Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) Inhibits prostaglandin synthesis centrally (COX in CNS), modulates descending serotonergic pathways and acts on the hypothalamic heat-regulating centre; weak peripheral anti-inflammatory action. Receptor / target profile: Central COX inhibition (peroxidase site) and actions of metabolite AM404 on TRPV1 and endocannabinoid systems; weak peripheral anti-inflammatory activity.
Hepatic – CYP2C9 to 4'-hydroxyaceclofenac (main), small amounts of diclofenac
Summary: Rapid, complete absorption; Tmax 1.25–3 h. >99% protein bound. Metabolised to 4'-hydroxyaceclofenac and diclofenac (CYP2C9). Half-life ~4 h.
Hepatic – glucuronidation, sulfation; ~5–10% CYP2E1 to NAPQI
Summary: Rapidly absorbed; Tmax 0.5–1 h. Glucuronidated and sulfated; small fraction via CYP2E1 to toxic NAPQI (detoxified by glutathione). Half-life 1–3 h.

Aceclofenac: Take after food or with milk; avoid alcohol (GI bleeding).
Paracetamol (Acetaminophen): With or without food; avoid alcohol.
Aceclofenac: BP, renal function, LFTs and CBC on prolonged use; signs of GI bleeding.
Paracetamol (Acetaminophen): LFTs if high doses long-term or risk factors.

Aceclofenac: Nausea, vomiting, epigastric pain, GI bleeding, renal failure, convulsions (rare). Supportive care; activated charcoal. Paracetamol (Acetaminophen): Potentially fatal hepatic necrosis; early symptoms may be absent. Give N-acetylcysteine as per nomogram – urgent treatment.
Randomised Indian trials show faster analgesic onset with the combination than aceclofenac alone in musculoskeletal pain.
Do not combine with other painkillers containing NSAIDs
Report black stools, vomiting blood, chest pain, swelling
Use for the shortest time needed
Do not exceed 4 g/day from all sources
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
